applied_note_updates.Exodus 21:17: Native Clementine Vulgate Exodus 21:17 places cursing parents here (mapping to Saints.Bible 21:16; kidnapping stands at native 21:16, mapping to Saints.Bible 21:17).

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Exod 21:16-17: replaced stale contradictory pre-migration order note on 21:17 so it agrees with native 21:16-17 and note 21:16.

applied_note_updates.Numbers 10:35: Native Clementine Vulgate Numbers 10:35 places the lifting up of the ark here (mapping to Saints.Bible 10:34; see note on 10:34).
applied_note_updates.Numbers 10:36: Native Clementine Vulgate Numbers 10:36 maps to Saints.Bible 10:35, and renders "multitude of the army of Israel" (multitudinem exercitus Israël) where the Hebrew has "ten thousands of the thousands of Israel."

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Num 10:34-36: replaced stale contradictory pre-migration note on 10:35 and moved the "multitudinem exercitus Israël" lexical gloss to native 10:36 where it actually occurs.

applied_note_updates.Numbers 26:17: The Vulgate names Gad's seventh son 'Ariel' (with the 'Arielites') and his fifth son 'Her' ('Er' in v. 16, matching Judah's son in v. 19), whereas the Masoretic Text has 'Areli' ('Arelites') and 'Eri'; likewise, Latin 'Selaitarum' (v. 20, 'Shelahites') and 'Phuaitarum' (v. 23, 'Puahites') lack the '-n-' of Hebrew 'Shelanites' and 'Punites.'
applied_note_updates.Numbers 26:19: In native Clementine Vulgate Numbers 26, Judah stands at vv. 19-22 after Gad (vv. 15-18), followed by Issachar (vv. 23-25) and Zebulun (vv. 26-27), matching the Hebrew tribal sequence (in Saints.Bible Septuagint-aligned order, Judah begins at 26:15 and Gad stands at 26:24-27).
applied_note_updates.Numbers 26:39: The Vulgate reads 'Supham' ('Shupham') rather than the Masoretic Text's longer form 'Shephupham,' and in v. 40 reads 'Noëmanitarum' ('Naamanites'), retaining the '-n-' where the Masoretic Text has 'Naamites.'

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Num 26:15-44: updated stale pre-migration tribe order and internal verse references in notes 26:17, 26:19, and 26:39.

applied_note_updates.Nehemiah 4:6: Native Vulgate Nehemiah 4:1-5 map to Saints.Bible 3:33-37, native 4:6 corresponds to MT 3:38 (unmatched in Saints.Bible), and native 4:7-23 map to Saints.Bible 4:1-17. Latin usque ad partem dimidiam literally reads "up to the half part" (half of its extent or height, without specifying altitudo).
applied_note_updates.Nehemiah 4:12: The Vulgate construes the difficult final clause (ex omnibus locis quibus venerant ad nos) as identifying where the Jews had come from rather than quoting direct speech, and in v. 13 reads in ordinem ('in order') where the Hebrew has 'by families.'
applied_note_updates.Nehemiah 4:21: With the hortatory subjunctives faciamus ('let us do') and teneat ('let ... hold') and the pronoun nostrum ('of us'), the Vulgate continues Nehemiah's speech through v. 21 rather than shifting to past-tense narrative as in the Hebrew; similarly, v. 18 has plural verbs (ædificabant, et clangebant) rather than a singular trumpeter.

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Neh 4:6-21: updated shifted pre-migration internal verse refs in notes 4:12 (v. 7 -> v. 13) and 4:21 (v. 15 -> v. 21, v. 12 -> v. 18), and aligned note 4:6 with Saints.Bible Neh 3 max 3:37.

applied_note_updates.Leviticus 6:11: Vulgate distinctly adds "usque ad favillam consumi faciet" ("will cause them to be consumed down to fine ash"), distinguishing coarse charred ashes ("cineres", v. 10) from fine ash ("favillam"). Clementine "efferret" is an orthographic variant of future indicative "efferet".
applied_note_updates.Leviticus 6:21: Vulgate "calidam" ("hot") reflects a distinct reading from MT ("well-mixed" / "baked pieces"), and v. 22 "qui jure patri successerit" ("who succeeds his father by right") renders MT's "anointed priest in his place."

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Lev 6:10-22: updated shifted pre-migration internal refs in notes 6:11 (v. 3 -> v. 10) and 6:21 (v. 15 -> v. 22).

applied_note_updates.1 Chronicles 6:31: The Vulgate reads 'super cantores' ('over the singers') and 'ex quo collocata est arca' ('from the time the ark was set in place') where the Hebrew has 'over the service of song' and 'after the ark had rest'; likewise, v. 32 has 'tabernaculo testimonii' ('the tabernacle of the testimony') for Hebrew 'the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.'
applied_note_updates.1 Chronicles 6:55: Here and throughout vv. 55-81, the Vulgate renders the open lands surrounding Levitical cities as 'suburbana' ('outskirts') where the Hebrew has 'pasturelands.'

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX 1 Chr 6:31-81: updated shifted pre-migration internal refs in notes 6:31 (v. 17 -> v. 32) and 6:55 (vv. 40-66 -> vv. 55-81).

applied_note_updates.1 Maccabees 1:51: Native Clementine Vulgate 1 Maccabees 1:51 combines the clauses of Saints.Bible/Greek 1:48 and 1:49 ("so that they would forget the law and alter all the ordinances of God"); native 1:48-50 map to Saints.Bible 1:45b-47, and native 1:52 onward map to Saints.Bible 1:50 onward.

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX 1 Macc 1:48-52: replaced stale pre-migration note falsely claiming v. 49 is omitted in Vulgate numbering with accurate native 1:51 -> Saints 1:48-49 mapping.

applied_note_updates.Acts 14:11: Here and in verse 12, the Vulgate renders the Greek deity names Zeus and Hermes with their Roman equivalents, Jupiter (Jovem/Jovis) and Mercury (Mercurium).

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Acts 14:11-12: updated shifted pre-migration internal ref in note 14:11 (verse 13 -> verse 12, where Sacerdos Jovis stands).

applied_note_updates.Psalms 2:7: Editorial policy review (Rule 4 / LAT-HQ-POL-04): Clem1598-USFX prints lowercase 'me' and 'te' (with 'Filius' capitalized only as the opening word after the colon); capitalization of "Me," "My Son," and "You" reflects traditional Messianic interpretation (cf. Acts 13:33; Heb 1:5) alongside the historical royal coronation reading ("me," "my son," "you").
applied_note_updates.Ephesians 4:23: Latin bare ablative 'spiritu mentis vestræ' ("in the spirit of your mind") has no preposition and can be understood either locatively of the renewed human inner spirit ("in the spirit of your mind") or instrumentally of the divine Spirit ("by the Spirit of your mind").

rationale: Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Ps 2:7 (Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu; ego hodie genui te.): added neutral Rule 4 / LAT-HQ-POL-04 editorial note matching Ps 2:2 without altering verse text. Verified directly in Clem1598-USFX Eph 4:23 (Renovamini autem spiritu mentis vestræ,): added neutral Rule 4 ambiguity note preserving both locative human-spirit and instrumental divine-Spirit readings without altering verse text.
